statement: This file plans how the data of the stateful units the draft moves is carried to STACKIT, for the families of data stores that have a planner (families). It moves no data and opens no connection: every step is for a person. A number in it is the customer's own statement (origin CUSTOMER_INPUT, with the answer it came from) or it is UNKNOWN; a quantity nobody stated is never zero. A duration is a lower bound of the transfer alone and a comparison with the accepted downtime says only whether that bound exceeds it, never that the window fits. Stateful units of other families have no plan here.

verification.what: Record the point after which a rollback loses data. Until the first of the writes that the target database accepts after the switch, a rollback is only the connection settings put back: the source database was not changed after the freeze and is current to it. From that write on, what the target database holds exists only there: it is copied back to the source database with a method rehearsed before the window, or accepted as lost. Once the source database is retired (its retirement step, after the GO and the retention the owner decides) there is nothing to go back to.
verification.expected: before the window the owner records the date until which the source database is kept, the method that copies the writes of the target database back or the decision that they are lost, and who calls the rollback
verification.manual_reason: how long the source is kept and whether the writes made on the target are copied back or lost are decisions of the owner of the application: the source states neither, so the plan names the limit and no date
not_provided: the date until which the source database is kept
the method that copies the writes of the target database back, or the decision that they are lost

checks.detail: the source is MySQL line 8.0 and STACKIT has no managed MySQL: the target is a different engine (MariaDB 10.11), not a version of the same one. For MySQL 8.0 the MariaDB documentation lists what differs: the JSON data type of MariaDB is an alias for LONGTEXT (the -> and ->> operators are not supported), GTIDs are not compatible, roles cannot authenticate, a user created with MySQL's SHA256 password algorithm cannot be used, and CREATE TABLESPACE is not supported.
checks.evidence: STACKIT MariaDB, Lifecycle (https://docs.stackit.cloud/products/databases/mariadb/reference/lifecycle/, last updated Jul 21, 2026): the versions are 10.11 (released December 2024) and 10.6 (end of life 01.07.2027); MariaDB documentation, Incompatibilities and Feature Differences Between MariaDB 10.11 and MySQL 8.0 (https://mariadb.com/docs/release-notes/community-server/about/compatibility-and-differences/incompatibilities-and-feature-differences-between-mariadb-10-11-and-mysql-8): "MariaDB's JSON data type is an alias for LONGTEXT"; "does not support MySQL's JSON operators (-> and ->>)"; "MariaDB never allows authentication via roles, while MySQL permits this"; "MariaDB's GTID is not compatible with MySQL's"; "does not support CREATE TABLESPACE for InnoDB"; "Users created with MySQL's SHA256 password algorithm cannot be used in" MariaDB; MariaDB documentation, MariaDB versus MySQL - Compatibility (https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mariadb-vs-mysql-compatibility/): MariaDB 10.2, 10.3 and 10.4 "function as limited drop-in replacements for MySQL 5.7, as far as InnoDB is concerned. However, the implementation differences continue to grow in each new MariaDB version"; AWS Aurora User Guide, Checking Aurora MySQL version numbers (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Updates.Versions.html): the engine version has the form {mysql-major-version}.mysql_aurora.{aurora-mysql-version}, "The {mysql-major-version} portion is 5.7 or 8.0" ("Aurora MySQL version 2 and 3 ... compatible with MySQL 5.7 or 8.0")

assets.rollback: Before the clients are switched nothing is switched: the source cache was neither stopped nor changed after the freeze, so it is current to the freeze; stop the writers, put the recorded connection settings of the source back and start the writers on it. After the switch, what was written to the target is not on the source: the point of no return is the first write to the target. The way back is a copy in the other direction (a separate rehearsal) or accepting the loss; take that decision before the window. This plan defines no reverse replication. Keep the source cache until the cause is known and do not delete it in the same hour; the STACKIT backups of the target (every 4 hours, 14 days) restore into the same instance only.
